turns.content:
hey, so last night was sam's birthday dinner at that ramen place on milwaukee. mostly chill, good group. but one of sam's friends, clara, was weirdly frosty the whole time. ignored me and julian when we said hi, made a pointed comment like "oh, you two can leave if you have other plans," and then rushed everyone on the walk after while stopping to take selfies. :-\

i'm not upset, just mildly annoyed. the rest of the night was fine. my question is — is this even worth mentioning to julian? or am i making a mountain out of a molehill? i'm tabling this until sunday afternoon at the earliest, i want my saturday drama-free and want to see if the irritation fades on its own. just trying to think it through.

Small molehill, and your Sunday-afternoon plan is exactly the right move for it.

Here's the thing that reframes it, though: Julian was *there*. He got iced out at hello too. So mentioning it isn't "bringing drama," it's just comparing notes with the other person who was on the receiving end. That's a very different bar than, say, texting Sam about it (which I would not do — Clara is Sam's friend, it was Sam's night, and nothing here rises to the level of "your friend was rude to us").

If it's still poking at you Sunday, a totally low-key "hey, was Clara being weird with us or was I imagining it?" is fine. Best case, Julian goes "oh yeah, totally, what was that" and you both get to be mildly annoyed together for four minutes and move on. Or he says "eh, didn't notice," and that's useful calibration too. Either way it's a two-minute conversation, not a Whole Thing.

One thing worth holding loosely: frosty-and-rushing-everyone-while-stopping-for-selfies reads a lot like someone having their own off night and managing it badly, rather than a targeted campaign against you two. The "you can leave if you have other plans" line is the only bit that seems actually pointed, and even that could be a clumsy joke that landed wrong. Not saying you have to extend grace, just that "Clara was in a mood" is probably the simplest explanation, and it's also the one that requires zero action from you.

Enjoy your drama-free Saturday. There's a decent chance this is a shrug by Sunday.

yeah, that's a fair read. "clara was in a mood" is probably the simplest explanation. i guess the part that sticks with me is why direct the "you can leave" at us specifically. but maybe she's just awkward. :-/

either way, my saturday's booked — coffee, bike ride, no drama. just trying to get a read on whether bringing it up at all is worth it, or if it makes me look like i'm dwelling.

Bringing it up once, casually, doesn't read as dwelling. Dwelling is bringing it up three times, or texting Julian a paragraph about it tonight instead of going on your bike ride. A one-liner on Sunday like "okay, was Clara weird with us or was it just me?" reads as *checking your read against his*, which is a pretty normal, secure thing to do. Honestly it comes off less dwell-y than silently carrying it around wondering.

The "why us specifically" piece: a few boring possibilities. You and Julian arrived as a unit, so you're the easy "you two" to address. Or you glanced at a phone / mentioned something else going on and she latched onto it. Or she's the type who's protective of Sam's attention and reads plus-ones as competition. None of those are about you being a problem. And if she's just awkward, awkward people often produce exactly this: a jab that sounds targeted but was really just the first thing that came out.

If you want a tiebreaker: if it's faded to a shrug by Sunday, let it go and don't mention it. If it's still nagging, mention it once, get Julian's take, and let that be the end of it. Either way you're fine.

Go enjoy the ride.

yeah, that makes sense. checking my read against his is the right way to frame it.

i guess i'm wondering — if i say nothing, does that read as letting someone be weird without consequence? or is that overthinking it. :-|

That's the overthinking part, yeah. Gently.

Two things are getting tangled: telling Julian, and Clara facing a consequence. Those aren't connected. Julian isn't Clara's manager. Whether you compare notes with him on Sunday or never mention it, Clara's night is identical either way. So the "letting it slide" worry doesn't actually attach to the Julian decision at all.

The only paths that *would* be a consequence are telling Sam or saying something to Clara directly, and you already correctly filed both under "not worth it." One frosty evening from a friend-of-a-friend doesn't need enforcement. It just needs to not happen again, and if it does, *then* you've got a pattern and a reason to say something. Right now you've got a data point.

Also, saying nothing isn't the same as letting it go unnoticed. You noticed. You clocked it, you'll clock it again if she does it next time, and you'll be a little more guarded around her. That's the consequence, and it's the proportional one for something this small.

So: Sunday check-in with Julian if it's still itching, purely to see if he saw what you saw. Not as a verdict on Clara. Then go be smug about your drama-free weekend.

yeah, i think you're right that they're separate things. telling julian isn't handing clara a consequence. :-)

i'll let it sit til sunday. if it's still there, one quick check-in with him. if not, shrug.

thanks for talking it through.

Sounds like a plan. And a very reasonable one — you basically talked yourself into the right answer, I just held the flashlight.

Enjoy the coffee and the ride. Sunday-you can deal with Clara, or more likely, forget she exists.
yeah. i think i'm settled on that. sunday check-in if it sticks, otherwise let it go. thanks for talking it through :-)
Anytime. Have a good Saturday — go earn that no-drama badge.
